subject: Order Form expiry carveouts, auto-renew mechanics and TF C exceptions
body:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@everwell.com>, Everwell Legal <legal@everwell.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form expiry carveouts, auto-renew mechanics and TF C exceptions

Hi Samir / Everwell Legal team,

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. Attaching our latest draft (Everwell_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx) — highlights below so legal can quickly see the tradeoffs we discussed: 

Key asks from Redwood (summary):
- Auto-renew mechanics: baseline 12-month renewal term; auto-renew unless either party gives notice within the notice window. We propose 60-day notice for paid, production contracts; 30-day notice for pilots / proof-of-value under $100k TCV.
- Term length definition: term begins on Commencement Date (defined as first day of service) and renews in 12-month increments.
- Termination for Convenience (TFC): Redwood is willing to accept a limited TFC but requests a 90-day transition period with service-level support and an agreed pro-rata credit for unused prepaid capacity. TFC should not apply during an initial onboarding ramp period (first 6 months) except for material breach.
- Early-termination fee: we can discuss a ramped fee schedule for multi-year commitments; proposed structure in autoresheet (autorenew_calcs.xlsx).

Attached: Everwell_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx (redlines highlighted) and the cost model (autorenew_calcs.xlsx).

Next steps I suggest: legal teams exchange redlines by close of business Thursday (07/22) so procurement has time for internal review next week. If any of the compromise points above are a non-starter, flag them in your reply and we will escalate to execs for tradeoffs.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Director, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@everwell.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Everwell Legal <legal@everwell.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form expiry carveouts, auto-renew mechanics and TF C exceptions

Marcus — thanks for the summary and the attachments. Quick reactions from Everwell Legal after an initial pass: 

1) Notice window: 30 days feels short for us for a production agreement. We need 90 days for auto-renew opt-out on multi-year/mission-critical pieces; open to 60 days for pilots. Please explain why Redwood prefers 60 vs 90 for production.

2) Definition of Commencement Date: we prefer the Commencement Date to be the date the first API key is activated and used in production (not simply seat creation). Please add explicit language tying it to production availability.

3) TFC: Everwell can accept a TFC but not within the first 12 months of a committed term unless Redwood agrees to an off-ramp credit equal to 25% of remaining monthly recurring charges. We will not accept unlimited TFC rights otherwise.

4) Transition support: we need a binding statement of transition assistance (30 days minimum) and access to audit logs during offboarding.

We will circulate redlines by Thursday as requested, but flagging these items now so your team can assess.

-- Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Vendor Contracts | Everwell Health
samir.patel@everwell.com | +1 202-555-0124

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@everwell.com>, Everwell Legal <legal@everwell.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 18:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form expiry carveouts, auto-renew mechanics and TF C exceptions

Samir — appreciate the early read. A few counterpoints from Redwood legal/ops to keep the conversation moving: 

- Notice window rationale: operationally we size capacity and reserved pool commitments based on expected renewal cadence. 60 days is a middle ground that reduces operational churn while still giving customers time to decide. For healthcare/multi-region customers we can agree to 90 days if Everwell provides an uplift on committed capacity pricing (we can propose a 5% uplift or an agreed minimum commitment).

- Commencement Date: acceptable to tie to first production API call. We'll insert language that requires Redwood to notify Everwell when production keys are enabled and provide a 10-day cure period for activation issues.

- TFC: Redwood cannot accept an unrestricted 25% off-ramp for all TFC instances. Proposed compromise: TFC allowed after the first 6 months of a 12-month term only if Redwood is paid a facilitation fee equal to 15% of the remaining recurring charges OR Redwood provides transition credits capped at 20% if the customer self-serves the migration. For customers that need a deeper transition we will provide 30 days of hands-on transition support and a prorated credit schedule.

- Audit logs: we will commit to exportable audit logs for the 90-day offboarding window but need to define retention and redaction rules (PHI considerations). Naomi, can you confirm data retention template we should propose for Everwell?

If these tradeoffs look workable Samir, Marcus and I can produce a tracked-change doc with the proposed language by Wednesday EOD. If not, let's set a 30-minute legal call to lock terms.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0199

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@everwell.com>, Everwell Legal <legal@everwell.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form expiry carveouts, auto-renew mechanics and TF C exceptions

Samir — appreciate the clarity.

Short plan:
1) Redwood agrees to amend the Commencement Date language to: "Commencement Date = date of first production API call (as evidenced by production API key activation and usage)."
2) Notice windows: propose the following split in Order Form: pilots (<$100k): 30-day opt-out; production: 60-day opt-out; mission-critical / multi-region: 90-day opt-out with a 5% capacity uplift (negotiable).
3) TFC: accept a limited TFC but with the compromise Karthik proposed: no TFC in first 6 months; thereafter, either a 15% facilitation fee OR capped transition credit up to 20% if customer migrates without Redwood hands-on support.
4) Transition & logs: Redwood will provide 30 days of hands-on transition assistance for TFC exits where requested; exportable audit logs for a 90-day window subject to redaction rules for PHI and a separate data transfer fee if heavy export is required.

I will upload the committed tracked-change Order Form (v3 with the language above) to the SharePoint link and send a DocuSign package for signatures if Everwell is comfortable with the tradeoffs. Can we agree to a legal sign-off by Friday 07/23 to keep procurement timelines intact?

If yes, I'll prepare the DocuSign and ask Naomi to add the PHI/data retention paragraph into the redline.

Best,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Director, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182
